True Consonant Clusters

There is a cluster hiding in กลัว, the word for afraid in your Week 2 pack. ก and ล blend into a single onset there, and I think spotting that pattern will quietly unlock a lot of similar words when you come across them.

A true cluster means both consonants are pronounced together, with no vowel slipped in between them. Take ปลา, fish. You say “plaa” in one blended push, mid tone, because ป is mid class and the syllable is live with no mark. The ล is fully sounded, but its own low class plays no part in the tone at all.

That last part is the part I would hold onto. Tone runs on the first consonant only, even when a vowel sign or a tone mark is written over the second one. ขวา, right side, shows why it matters: ข is high class, so ขวา rises, and if you classed it by the ว instead you would land on mid and get it wrong. กว่า, more than, works the same way from the other side, with its mai ek sitting over the ว while the low tone still comes from mid-class ก.

For tomorrow morning I would keep it to three words: ปลา, กลัว, and ขวา. Say the cluster first, name the first consonant’s class, then read the whole word. If ขวา comes out rising, you have the new step, and the market and direction words that use these onsets will start looking much friendlier.

—Zerg
